edit.description: the walls the carry can raise, each stating the scope it is
the fold that abandons every waiting span, and the drain that goes on over an entry-scoped wall
the fate an entry-scoped merge failure rows as, beside the walled row that keeps its base and head
the merge-stage cases over a wall of each scope

summary: each merge-stage wall states its scope where it raises: an entry-scoped throw ends that span as a failed merge with its facts and the drain goes on; only a trunk-scoped one walls the wave
acceptance: every throw the merge stage can raise declares at its site whether it is one entry's or the trunk's; an entry-scoped one is that span's failed merge, reported with its facts, and every sibling whose agent finished and whose gates passed is still carried; only a trunk-scoped one abandons the wave
tests: an entry-scoped merge throw ends that span and the wave carries its siblings
a trunk-scoped merge throw abandons the spans still waiting
pins: an abandoned span is still rowed with the base and head it could be carried again from
notes: The row's own doc says the fold is keyed on the wave being walled and never on the cause, so a refusal scoped to one slug costs every sibling its span. The blockers delete the marker write, the rewind and the foreign-tip guard, leaving: a ledger rewrite that refused (trunk's), a prior-attempt record the store refused (one entry's), a failed tip read. A gate's throw already has this rule (`spec/chain.md`, *What a gate returns*); the merge stage has none.
